title: Everyday English
description: Find your voice in familiar moments, from meeting a neighbor to making weekend plans. Build a foundation with useful questions, friendly requests, and clear sentences about daily life.

chapters.title: A friendly start
chapters.description: Introduce yourself, welcome someone, and ask simple questions.

sentences.text: Hello, I am new here.
sentences.hint: Greet someone as a newcomer.

sentences.text: I am your new neighbor.
sentences.hint: Explain that you recently moved nearby.

sentences.text: It is nice to meet you.
sentences.hint: Show pleasure at a first introduction.

sentences.text: What is your name?
sentences.hint: Ask what to call someone.

sentences.text: Are you from this town?
sentences.hint: Ask whether someone comes from the local area.

sentences.text: This is my friend.
sentences.hint: Introduce a person you know well.

sentences.text: Please sit next to me.
sentences.hint: Invite someone to take the seat beside you.

sentences.text: Do you want some water?
sentences.hint: Offer someone a simple drink.

sentences.text: You are in the right place.
sentences.hint: Reassure someone that they found the correct location.

sentences.text: I am happy to be here.
sentences.hint: Say you feel good about being present.

chapters.title: A good morning
chapters.description: Describe waking up, getting dressed, and leaving home.

sentences.text: I get up at seven o'clock.
sentences.hint: Give the time you leave your bed.

sentences.text: My alarm is very loud.
sentences.hint: Describe a strong wake-up sound.

sentences.text: I open the curtains.
sentences.hint: Let daylight in through the window.

sentences.text: The bathroom is across the hall.
sentences.hint: Explain where to find the washroom.

sentences.text: I brush my teeth before breakfast.
sentences.hint: Describe cleaning your teeth before the morning meal.

sentences.text: These socks are clean.
sentences.hint: Say this pair is ready to wear.

sentences.text: Where is my blue shirt?
sentences.hint: Ask for help finding a piece of clothing.

sentences.text: I don't drink coffee in the morning.
sentences.hint: Explain which drink is not part of your routine.

sentences.text: My bag is ready by the door.
sentences.hint: Say your packed things are near the exit.

sentences.text: We leave the house together.
sentences.hint: Describe going out at the same time.

chapters.title: At the table
chapters.description: Talk about food, express preferences, and ask for what you need.

sentences.text: I am hungry.
sentences.hint: Say you need something to eat.

sentences.text: There is some bread on the table.
sentences.hint: Point out food available on the dining surface.

sentences.text: We have eggs for breakfast.
sentences.hint: Describe a food in your morning meal.

sentences.text: Do you like fresh tomatoes?
sentences.hint: Ask about someone's taste in vegetables.

sentences.text: My soup is too hot.
sentences.hint: Say your bowl needs time to cool.

sentences.text: I would like a glass of milk.
sentences.hint: Politely ask for a dairy drink.

sentences.text: Please pass the rice.
sentences.hint: Ask someone to move a dish toward you.

sentences.text: There isn't any cheese in the fridge.
sentences.hint: Explain that a chilled dairy food has run out.

sentences.text: How many apples do we need?
sentences.hint: Ask for the number of fruits required.

sentences.text: This meal tastes good.
sentences.hint: Say you enjoy the flavor of the food.

chapters.title: A place called home
chapters.description: Describe rooms, locate belongings, and make simple household requests.

sentences.text: Our home has two bedrooms.
sentences.hint: Give the number of sleeping rooms where you live.

sentences.text: The keys are on the kitchen shelf.
sentences.hint: Explain where to find the items that unlock doors.

sentences.text: There is a lamp beside the sofa.
sentences.hint: Locate a light next to the couch.

sentences.text: The window is open.
sentences.hint: Say that air can come in from outside.

sentences.text: Can you close the door, please?
sentences.hint: Politely ask someone to shut the entrance.

sentences.text: My room is small but bright.
sentences.hint: Describe a little space with plenty of light.

sentences.text: We keep our shoes under the stairs.
sentences.hint: Explain the usual storage place for footwear.

sentences.text: I clean the floor on Saturdays.
sentences.hint: Describe a weekly household chore.

sentences.text: The washing machine is in the kitchen.
sentences.hint: Locate the appliance used for laundry.

sentences.text: Please turn off the light.
sentences.hint: Ask someone to stop the lamp from shining.

chapters.title: Around the neighborhood
chapters.description: Find local places, buy everyday items, and ask about payment.

sentences.text: The bakery is near the park.
sentences.hint: Locate the bread shop beside a green space.

sentences.text: I need a loaf of bread.
sentences.hint: Name a basic item on your shopping list.

sentences.text: How much is this notebook?
sentences.hint: Ask the price of something to write in.

sentences.text: The post office opens at nine.
sentences.hint: Give the starting time for postal services.

sentences.text: Can I pay by card?
sentences.hint: Ask whether cash is necessary.

sentences.text: I am looking for the bus stop.
sentences.hint: Explain that you need the place to catch a bus.

sentences.text: This bag is too heavy.
sentences.hint: Say something is difficult to carry because of its weight.

sentences.text: The shop is closed on Sundays.
sentences.hint: Explain which day the store does not serve customers.

sentences.text: Please give me a receipt.
sentences.hint: Ask for written proof of your purchase.

sentences.text: I can walk home from here.
sentences.hint: Say you can return on foot.

chapters.title: Finding the time
chapters.description: Use clock times, days, and frequency to organize daily life.

sentences.text: What time is it now?
sentences.hint: Ask someone to check the clock.

sentences.text: My class starts at half past ten.
sentences.hint: Say your lesson begins at ten thirty.

sentences.text: We have lunch at noon.
sentences.hint: Give midday as the time for your meal.

sentences.text: I am usually early.
sentences.hint: Say you tend to arrive before the expected time.

sentences.text: The bus comes every twenty minutes.
sentences.hint: Describe the regular gap between bus arrivals.

sentences.text: Is the library open this afternoon?
sentences.hint: Check whether you can visit the book-lending place later today.

sentences.text: My appointment is on Tuesday.
sentences.hint: Name the day of a scheduled meeting.

sentences.text: We don't work on weekends.
sentences.hint: Explain that Saturday and Sunday are days off.

sentences.text: I have five minutes before the next bus.
sentences.hint: Say there is only a short wait for your ride.

sentences.text: Let's meet outside at six.
sentences.hint: Suggest a time and an outdoor meeting place.

chapters.title: Feeling well
chapters.description: Describe common symptoms, ask for help, and talk about healthy routines.

sentences.text: I don't feel well today.
sentences.hint: Say that you are not feeling healthy.

sentences.text: My throat hurts.
sentences.hint: Describe pain in the part you use to swallow.

sentences.text: Do you have a headache?
sentences.hint: Ask whether someone has pain in their head.

sentences.text: I need to sit down.
sentences.hint: Say you must stop standing for a moment.

sentences.text: Please drink some water.
sentences.hint: Encourage someone to have a simple drink.

sentences.text: The doctor is free this morning.
sentences.hint: Say a medical professional has time to see someone today.

sentences.text: I take a short walk every day.
sentences.hint: Describe a little daily exercise on foot.

sentences.text: You look tired.
sentences.hint: Notice that someone seems to need rest.

sentences.text: I go to bed early when I am ill.
sentences.hint: Describe getting extra rest during sickness.

sentences.text: I feel better after a good night's sleep.
sentences.hint: Explain that sleeping well helps you recover.

chapters.title: Family and friends
chapters.description: Talk about relationships, shared activities, and what people are doing now.

sentences.text: My sister lives near us.
sentences.hint: Say a female sibling has a home close by.

sentences.text: Our grandparents have a small garden.
sentences.hint: Describe an outdoor space belonging to older relatives.

sentences.text: Who is the person in this photo?
sentences.hint: Ask someone to identify a face in a picture.

sentences.text: That is my brother's bicycle.
sentences.hint: Explain which relative owns the bike.

sentences.text: My parents are cooking dinner.
sentences.hint: Say your mother and father are preparing the evening meal.

sentences.text: The children are playing in the yard.
sentences.hint: Describe young people having fun outside the house.

sentences.text: I call my cousin every week.
sentences.hint: Describe a regular phone conversation with a relative.

sentences.text: We often help each other.
sentences.hint: Say you regularly give and receive support.

sentences.text: Can your friend join us for lunch?
sentences.hint: Ask whether another person can share your midday meal.

sentences.text: I like spending time with my family.
sentences.hint: Say you enjoy being with your relatives.

chapters.title: Whatever the weather
chapters.description: Describe the sky, choose clothes, and compare everyday weather conditions.

sentences.text: It is cold outside today.
sentences.hint: Describe a low outdoor temperature.

sentences.text: The sky is clear this morning.
sentences.hint: Say there are no clouds at the start of the day.

sentences.text: Is it raining now?
sentences.hint: Ask whether water is falling from the sky.

sentences.text: You need a warm coat.
sentences.hint: Recommend clothing that protects against the cold.

sentences.text: I can't find my umbrella.
sentences.hint: Say your protection from the rain is missing.

sentences.text: We stay inside on very hot days.
sentences.hint: Describe avoiding the outdoors in strong heat.

sentences.text: The wind is strong near the river.
sentences.hint: Describe air blowing hard beside the water.

sentences.text: It is warmer in the kitchen than in the hall.
sentences.hint: Compare the temperatures in two parts of the house.

sentences.text: There is snow on the roof.
sentences.hint: Describe a white winter covering on top of a building.

sentences.text: It is sunny, but the air is still cold.
sentences.hint: Explain that bright weather does not always mean warmth.

chapters.title: Small plans
chapters.description: Suggest activities, arrange a meeting, and explain simple future plans.

sentences.text: I am going to visit a friend tomorrow.
sentences.hint: Describe a social plan for the next day.

sentences.text: We want to have a picnic on Sunday.
sentences.hint: Suggest an outdoor meal at the end of the week.

sentences.text: Are you free after work?
sentences.hint: Check whether someone has time when their job finishes.

sentences.text: Let's buy some fruit for the picnic.
sentences.hint: Suggest getting fresh food for an outdoor meal.

sentences.text: I can bring a blanket.
sentences.hint: Offer to provide something to sit on or keep warm.

sentences.text: My brother is going to make sandwiches.
sentences.hint: Say a relative plans to prepare filled bread.

sentences.text: We don't need to take many things.
sentences.hint: Explain that only a few items are necessary.

sentences.text: Can we meet at the park entrance?
sentences.hint: Suggest gathering at the way into a green space.

sentences.text: I want to stay home tonight because I am tired.
sentences.hint: Give a need for rest as your reason not to go out.

sentences.text: We can make another plan for next week.
sentences.hint: Suggest arranging a different activity at a later date.
